text: The bay lies flat and warm under a moon nearly full, its surface unmarked by any serious wind. Lake Huron is near its annual high, and the shallows hold heat accumulated across two months of long days. Along the wet margins of Rifle River Road, joe-pye weed stands in full dusky-rose bloom, and goldenrod has begun to open gold along every fence line between Standish and the Thumb. Katydids are rasping in the oaks after dark. On the AuSable in the early morning hours, trico spinners are due above the riffles, the smallest of the season's hatches, falling spent on still water by mid-morning. Fourteen hours of daylight remain, but the number is shrinking. Walk a wet ditch edge near Bay City State Park in the next few days and find the joe-pye weed at its height.
